pr_title: Extract creation and last updated timestamp for v3 dump
pr_body:
# Pull Request

## Related issue
Fixes #2988

## What does this PR do?

Inspired by the v4 dump implementation, this extracts the first `createdAt` and last `updatedAt` fields by parsing the task queue.

Questions:
- Should the parsing of the tasks be cached instead of being parsed for every index since it might add a performance penalty?
- I am not sure if the `created_at` and `processed_at` fields are correct 
- Should I assume the data is sorted in some order like with `uuid` or `updateId`? I assumed the list is unordered.
- I was planning to populate my dev instance with data and dump my data. Is there a way to dump with previous versions?

## PR checklist
Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:
- [x] Does this PR fix an existing issue, or have you listed the changes applied in the PR description (and why they are needed)?
- [x] Have you read the contributing guidelines?
- [x] Have you made sure that the title is accurate and descriptive of the changes?

Thank you so much for contributing to Meilisearch!
pr_comments:
@irevoire Thanks for the feedback.

>  The only three kind of tasks that can create an index.
> The documentAddition and Settings can create it even if they fails, they’ll do it anytime they starts processing the task

I changed the `meta.createdAt` and `meta.updatedAt` to use the `task.finishedAt` field instead of `task.enqueuedAt` as specified by your code sample and comment. Since only `finished` tasks have this value, I filtered for that as well. 

I also just took the earliest `createdAt` and latest `updatedAt` instead of depending on `updateId`

>  (On Index Deletion) We reset both markers

When an index is deleted, it uses a new id and resets the `updateId` so I don't think we need to reset anything.

Look like we brought the milli's issues on meilisearch with that merge :joy:

issue_context.title: Extract the dates ouf of the dumpv3
issue_context.body:
When importing a dump v3, we should extract the creation and last updated timestamp.
https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/blob/main/dump/src/reader/v3/mod.rs#L158-L177

The idea is to look at the whole task queue until you find the first task concerning your index (=last_updated_at), and you already have the task_uid of the task_creating it. Thus you then need to continue until you reach this task and extract its date as the creation_date.
comments: May I ask how one is theoritically supposed to find the task linked to an index - with the dumpv3 ? I can't find any real way to do that ...
